title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it: the same detection reads 'Confirmed' on one sub-tab and 'New' on the next
evidence_file_line: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_alert_provider.dart:928 — `return overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state;` inside `resolveTransientAlertState`, the shared resolver every alert surface now goes through (transients_screen.dart:180 card state, :213/:219/:225 filter buckets; transient_alert_badge.dart:444; transient_alerts_panel.dart:131/:206-207; unacknowledgedAlertCountProvider transient_alert_provider.dart:950; headless transient_handlers.dart:76/:281/:347-351).
summary: STILL-OPEN check came back negative: the cause the adversarial verifier identified is gone in the tree today, and it was closed at the root rather than at one call site. The verifier's correction was authoritative — the bug was never 'the alert list is not invalidated' (transient_alert_provider.dart:553-556 does re-merge on every allTransientDetectionsProvider emission, and that provider is a live drift watch over transient_detections, so markReviewed re-emits); it was that the Observing Alerts UI read the `transientAlertStatesProvider` override map bare and fell back to `newAlert` on a miss, throwing away the `acknowledged` the mapper had already produced. A prior wave introduced `resolveTransientAlertState(alert, overrides) => overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state` and routed every consumer through it: the card's state, all three filter buckets, the status-bar badge dropdown, the suggestions panel (render + sort), the unacknowledged badge count, and the headless REST surface that serves mobile/web (which also stopped counting queued/dismissed off the raw override map). I audited every reader of `transientAlertStatesProvider` and of `TransientAlertState` in packages/ and apps/ and found no remaining bare read — the only non-resolving reads left are the notifier's own writes and `_countState`, whose comment scopes it to the mutation ACK responses that have no alert population in hand. A user action still wins over the row state, which is what an override is for, and API-sourced alerts default to newAlert so their behaviour is unchanged. Nothing changed in this task; the working tree is byte-identical to how I found it.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transients_confirmed_state_test.dart (3 tests, drives the real TransientsView with an alert produced by the production transientAlertFromDetection mapper: 'a confirmed detection is not badged New on Observing Alerts', 'an unreviewed detection is still New', 'a confirmed detection does not sit under the New filter') plus packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/alert_state_across_surfaces_test.dart (4 tests covering the suggestions panel and the status-bar dropdown). All 12 tests in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/ pass.
revert_check: Severed the wiring at the shared resolver: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_alert_provider.dart:928, `return overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state;` -> `return overrides[alert.id] ?? TransientAlertState.newAlert;` (the exact pre-fix semantics — the fallback that used to live in transient_card.dart:56). 4 tests failed, reproducing the finding's symptom verbatim: 'a confirmed detection is not badged New on Observing Alerts' reported Found 1 widget with text "New" descending from TransientCard; 'a confirmed detection does not sit under the New filter' reported the detection NS J132952.80+471124.0 still present under the New filter; both cross-surface tests reported Found 1 widget with text "NEW". Restored the line and reran: all 12 pass.
caveats: The one thing I could not exercise in-process is the live tab-switch timing (Confirm in First Light, then click across to Observing Alerts) — that is a StreamProvider.autoDispose re-subscription, not a pure widget test. I traced it instead: markReviewed writes transient_detections (transient_detections_dao.dart:241) -> watchRecentDetections declares readsFrom {transientDetections} (:73-79) so drift re-runs it -> _liveDetectionsFeed publishes a fresh read (transient_detections_provider.dart:214-221) -> activeTransientAlertsProvider's ref.listen re-merges (transient_alert_provider.dart:553-556) -> localFirstLightAlerts remaps through transientAlertFromDetection, whose state field is acknowledged when reviewed is set (transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70). Each link is present. Scope note: I checked only the direction the finding names (First Light row state -> alert surfaces). The reverse (dismissing on Observing Alerts writing back to the detection row) is NOT implemented — the override map is a separate store keyed 'firstlight:<id>' — but that is by design per the resolver's doc comment (a user action on the alert surface wins locally) and is not what this finding reported.
